chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Sayf ibn Amira who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you visits his brother (who is ill), let him (the patient) ask him (the visitor) to supplicate for him, for his supplication is like the supplication of the Angels.'

key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَة: The Angels, celestial beings who perpetually worship God; their supplications are considered especially meritorious
key_terms.دُعَاء: Supplication, du'a — a personal prayer or petition addressed to God
key_terms.عَائِداً: One who visits the sick (from 'awada, to return or revisit); sick-visiting (iyada) is a communal religious duty in Islam

ai.seo_question: Should a sick person ask their visitor to pray for them according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches an etiquette of sick-visiting (iyada): the sick person should actively request the visitor to make du'a on their behalf. The Imam gives a powerful rationale for this—the supplication of a sick visitor carries a special spiritual weight comparable to that of the Angels, whose prayers are known to be accepted by God. This teaching encourages the sick to seek intercession through visitors rather than bearing their affliction in silence, fostering mutual care within the Muslim community.
word_analysis: then let him (the patient) ask him (the visitor)

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Muhammad, from Sayf Bin Ameyra who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When one of you goes over to his brother as a visitor for him, so let him (the patient) ask him (the visitor) to supplicate for him, for his supplication is like a supplication of the Angels’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who has narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah, who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one of you visits his brother in belief during his illness, he should ask him (the patient) to pray for him; a patient’s prayer is like the prayer of the angels.’”
